data.narrative:
Rivan is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised $47.2M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine entities in the Climate & Energy sector—one public (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the narrow peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tiers to support a robust Peer-Median approach; only zero datapoints met the filtering criteria for median benchmarking.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable framework here. Using the $47.2M in total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $94.4M. This method assumes a standard progression in valuation multiples consistent with the risk-reduction profile of advancing stages, though it lacks peer-market calibration.

The triangulated range reflects these constraints: a low estimate of $80.2M (15% discount to the stage-progression result) and a high estimate of $109M (15% premium), anchoring to a median of $94.4M. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-set peer comps to validate the stage multiplier against market precedent and the reliance on total-raised-as-proxy rather than an explicit pre-money or post-money valuation. A full peer-median cross-check should be revisited as more same-stage or sector-peer data becomes available.
